chunks.text: The primary stage of wastewater treatment is the removal of both grit and primary sludge. Grit is represented in the model as solid-state silicon dioxide which is about 1% of the total inlet water flow. The grit in wastewater has a specific gravity in the range 1.5-2.7 kg/l which is much higher than that of the organic matter suspended in the influent stream (1.02 kg/l). A differential sedimentation can thus be a successful mechanism for separating grit from organic matter (Liu and Lipták, 2000) . A density-based classifier is defined as a unit operation to remove the grit in this model. The primary treatment can reduce the Total Suspended Solids (TSS) by 50-60%. Also, it implies the removal of the BOD in the incoming wastewater by 20-30%. The percentage of the sludge removal chosen in the present model is 55%.

It has a total height of 4 m, and occupies a surface area of 1500 m 2 and a volume of 6000 m 3 . The tank is fed from the 6th, treated water is harvested from the 10th, and the settled sludge flows out from the first layer. A fraction of the sludge flows out of the system in the form of waste at a flow rate of 385 m 3 /d, corresponding to a biomass age of 9 days, while the other fraction is recycled externally to the first tank at a rate of 18,446 m 3 /d. The biological processes occurring in both biological reactors are simulated using the IWA Activated Sludge Model No. 1 (ASM1) proposed by [47] . This model uses thirteen state variables to track the fate of biodegradable, non-biodegradable, soluble, insoluble, nitrogen, and carbon materials. These state variables are linked to eight degradation bioprocesses occurring in biological reactors.

chunks.text: This study was carried out using data from the advanced biological treatment plant in the eastern region of Kocaeli, Turkey. The construction area lies on latitude 40 • 45′04″ North and longitude 29 • 58′ 05″ East and covers 29.13 ha area, of which 0.24 ha is closed. The plant was designed to serve the equivalent population of 447,000 with 140,000 m 3 /day treatment capacity. Advanced biological treatment is implemented in the plant. Long aerated activated sludge process is utilized in which nitrogen and phosphorus removal along with carbon oxidation takes place. The flow chart of the plant is presented in Fig. 1 . As can be seen from Fig. 1 , the treatment plant consists of a succession of anaerobic, anoxic and aerobic tanks, a settling tank, and a sludge return connection transporting the settling sludge to the anaerobic tank inlet. Treatment sludge with high phosphorus content obtained as a result of treatment processes is disposed of in licensed facilities after being subjected to thickening, aerobic sludge digestion and dewatering processes.

chunks.text: The drying facility is located in a large Polish wastewater treatment plant and is composed of 4 lines. The scheme of one drying line is presented in Fig. 1 . Dewatered sludge is collected in a silo from where it is dosed to drum dryers. The temperature in the drum dryers is maintained at ca. 240-260 • C using hot oil. Sludge is uniformly distributed in the drum with paddles. The sludge retention time in the drier is 1-2 min, and the sludge layer in the drum is 1-2 cm thick. Water from the sludge is evaporated and flows as condensate with process air through a purification system composed of a Venturi orifice and two scrubbers, where it is then rinsed with the process water (secondary effluent from the wastewater treatment plant). chunks.text: Of 393 WWTFs in Colorado with active, pending, or recently withdrawn permits at the time of this study, 91 active facilities had design capacities >7570 m 3 d -1 and were selected for evaluation. Of the 91 WWTFs that met initial survey criteria, 18 treated industrial waste streams and did not possess AD and 3 were in the process of permanently closing. These 21 WWTFs were omitted from the analysis. During the study, one additional WWTF with a design flowrate <7570 m 3 d -1 using AD was identified and subsequently incorporated into the analysis. Of the 71 WWTFs examined, 61 (86%) provided feedback to the inquiry. The number of respondents to each question is indicated parenthetically for responses discussed. The majority of WWTFs in the study were located in large metropolitan centers and/or along the Rocky Mountain Front Range (Fig. 1 ). Many facilities in Colorado have design capacities much greater than their average annual flow, therefore, actual annual average flowrates were used for conducting analyses and discussing results.

chunks.text: Preliminary treatment is the initial stage where coarse particles and foreign matter commonly found in raw wastewater are removed to optimize subsequent treatment processes (Sonune and Ghate, 2004) . This stage involves activities such as coarse screening, grit removal, and the comminution of large objects in wastewater. Grit chambers maintain high water velocities, preventing organic compounds from settling within the chamber. Although not all wastewater treatment plants incorporate grit removal in their preliminary treatment, some employ comminutors alongside coarse screening to reduce the size of large particles. Additionally, flow measurement devices and wave flumes are commonly used during this phase (Pachwarya et al., 2021) . It's crucial to remove oil and grease from wastewater at this stage to mitigate its adverse effects on the subsequent treatment processes. This is typically achieved through methods such as chlorination, vacuum flotation, and aeration (Pachwarya et al., 2021) .

chunks.text: The secondary biological treatment consists of two carrousel-shaped biological reactors with suspended biomass, equipped with two horizontal aerators, which include nitrogen removal. Regarding the sludge line, a fraction of the solids settled in the secondary settler is purged to the sludge thickener. Previously to the band filter, the sludge passes through a homogenizer to be mixed with cationic polyelectrolyte and further dewatered in the band filter prior being stored in a silo. Calafell WWTP was built on 1994 to treat the wastewaters of the municipalities of Calafell and Bellveí and designed for 70,000 population equivalent with a maximum flow of 12,000 m 3 /day. After a primary treatment, wastewater is treated in two activated sludge reactors with extended aeration including nitrogen removal, followed by the secondary settler. From these units, the treated wastewater is directly discharged to the submarine sewage. Some differences are observed in the operation of the plant between winter and summer seasons due to fluctuations on the population and changes on the influent composition. A coagulation-flocculation treatment, only operated during summer, receives the wastewater after the screening step.

Water quality data and ammonia discharge limit data for the case studies is provided in Table SI-3. It should be noted that all sites were regulated and in compliance to meet monthly (cBOD) and total suspended solids (TSS) emissions of less than 30 mg/L and 80 mg/L, respectively; whereas minimum ammonia emissions varied 0.22-13.7 mg/L depending on the receiving water body characteristics. chunks.text: Screening, sedimentation, and skimming are considered pretreatment mechanisms in common wastewater treatment systems. Screening, one of the oldest types of physical treatment, denotes the removal of large and floating solid materials that may create a blockage in the upcoming treatment processes (Naidoo and Olaniran, 2014) . Screening is a must in wastewater treatment to ensure the efficient functioning of different technologies by prohibiting potential damage, blockage, and process interruption. Depending on the types of eliminated contaminants, screening can be of two types: fine screening and coarse screening. Coarse screening manually or mechanically removes large solids, debris, and rags which are more than 6 mm, whereas fine screening removes suspended solid materials which are 0.001-6 mm (Bhargava, 2016) . When screening is impractical or not suitable for a certain setup, then another physical process, comminution is usually adopted. In this process, the solid materials are crushed into pieces using different types of cutters. Such cutters are usually installed in between the grit chamber and the sedimentation tank. The crushed materials are then precipitated and isolated from the wastewater (Chauhan and Kumar, 2020) .

chunks.text: Plant C used the intermittent cycle extended aeration process (ICEAS) with continuous inflow/intermittent outflow and no internal/external reflux as a secondary treatment. Plant E used the University of Cape Town (UCT) process (in which the sludge from the settling tank is transferred into the anoxic tank rather than the anaerobic tank) as a secondary process. All five WWTPs used tertiary treatments such as coagulation/flocculation, filtration, and disinfection to remove total suspended solids (TSS), total phosphorus (TP), and pathogens. Plant A did not contain a coagulation/flocculation tank, and the secondary treatment effluent was fed directly into a D-type filter tank (Dean Corporation, China). The A 2 O process used in Plant B was performed using an anaerobic pond and a concentric cycle degradation pond in which the inner circle of the concentric circle was the anoxic zone and the outer ring was the aerobic zone. Plant B did not contain a coagulation/flocculation tank, but the long distance between the secondary sedimentation tank and tertiary filtration tank allowed space for the coagulant to be added and for the coagulant to mix and react with the wastewater.
